messages:
kevin: Quick follow-up from the spike: we prototyped a tiny control-plane sidecar that lives in customer VPCs and only proxies control/config traffic. It avoids peering but raises rollout/egress questions. Open to quick thoughts.

lina: Interesting. How do we keep it minimal? My brain says: no persistent secrets, local loopback API, unix socket for local agent, and strictly outbound mTLS to our cp.

samir: Agreed on minimality. Two immediate ops concerns: 1) customers requiring fixed egress IPs; 2) mass reconnect storms after network blips. Both need explicit mitigations.

anya: For egress IPs we can offer: self-managed NAT (customer-provided), managed egress we deploy into customer account, or keep peering as a premium. We should codify pricing/SLAs for managed-egress.

rachel: From infra/security: avoid long-lived keys. Use ephemeral certs with an attestation step (cloud metadata + sig) to mint a short-lived client cert. TTLs ~5m. Also require sidecar to present a signed image hash during bootstrap.

kevin: Implementation sketch: sidecar exposes 127.0.0.1:15060 and a unix socket at /var/run/rw-sidecar.sock for local SDKs. It performs local RBAC so only agent uid can use it. Outbound mTLS to cp.redwood.net:443. Config flags: egress_mode: [none, managed-egress, peering], telemetry_mode: [send-to-redwood, forward-to-customer, local-only].

lina: Add health endpoints: /healthz (local) and /ready (for our probes), plus an ops port for metrics (prom format) that can be scraped by customer's monitoring if they opt-in. Make metrics opt-in by default.

samir: For reconnect storms: we need jittered exponential backoff with randomization and global reconnect windows. Also a token refresh coordinator so not every sidecar refreshes at the same moment. Use TTL +/- random jitter.

anya: Rollout story: canary via customer opt-in first. Then staged auto-upgrades with percentage-based gating (5%, 25%, 100%) and automatic rollback on error-rate/latency thresholds. Provide a self-managed helm chart for customers who don't want auto-upgrades.

rachel: Security checklist (high level): no persistent keys, attestation + signed artifact verification, least-privilege IAM for any managed-egress infra, signed telemetry only with opt-in, and clear revocation path (revoke certs on compromise).

kevin: Migration playbook idea: for customers using peering today, give three paths: 1) keep peering (no change), 2) enable sidecar + peering for transition, 3) switch to sidecar + managed-egress. Provide a fallback policy so if sidecar can't reach cp, traffic goes to peering/relay depending on customer config.

lina: Also define compatibility with our Private offering: sidecar should be compatible with Private control plane when run in 'air-gapped' mode (no telemetry out; local-only logs). We'll need a mode switch and documentation.

samir: Performance notes from spike: p50 handshake ~16ms, p99 ~58ms under 2k simulated agents. Memory ~45-70MB. CPU low at idle. We should run a sustained 10k-agent soak and an outage/reconnect blast to validate backoff.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: sidecar-rollout-spike branch deployed to staging. CI: https://ci.internal/8901 build green :white_check_mark:

anya: Sales & legal implications: we need clear marketing language on what runs in customer accounts, who is responsible for patching, and what support tiers include. Managed-egress customers get SLA; self-managed are best-effort. Drafting a short doc.

rachel: One more: debugging primitives. Expose a secure admin socket that SOC can use (with 2FA) to retrieve diagnostics, but default is disabled unless customer explicitly allows. Avoid remote shell.

kevin: Agreed. Action items: Lina -> failure-mode + minimal network ACLs; Samir -> scale tests (5k/10k + outage blast); Anya -> sales/legal one-pager + pricing for managed-egress; Rachel -> security checklist + attestation flow; Kevin -> PoC helm chart and migration playbook. Revisit next Tues. :thumbsup:
